headline: Netflix shuts down two game studios, including Oxenfree creator Night School
summary: Netflix is making a bigger shift toward party games and titles streamed to TVs, leading to the closure of Night School Studio and Moonloot Games.
details: Netflix is reportedly shutting down two of its gaming studios, Night School Studio and Moonloot Games, as it pivots its strategy towards TV-based party games.

Night School Studio, known for the Oxenfree series, was acquired by Netflix in 2021. The studio recently released the horror experience Unhinged for TVs and a mobile game tied to Black Mirror in 2025. Helsinki-based Moonloot Games was established in 2022.

This move signifies a shift from Netflix's previous mobile-focused approach, which often featured prestige indie titles. The company is now concentrating on four key pillars: kids, party, narrative, and "mainstream" games.

Netflix spokesperson Chrissy Kelleher confirmed organizational changes to align with these new priorities, which include eliminating additional roles within its games business. Tara Voelker, who served as the "single accessibility person" on the gaming team, was among those affected.

This is not Netflix's first studio closure; the company previously shut down a studio behind a Squid Game mobile title, sold Cozy Grove studio Spry Fox back to its original owners, and closed a AAA studio in 2024 that never released a game.

headline_marked: [[ChatGPT for Mac adds opt-in Computer History feature]], replacing Chronicle
headline: ChatGPT for Mac adds opt-in Computer History feature, replacing Chronicle
summary: OpenAI is rolling out a new 'Computer History' feature for ChatGPT and Codex on Mac, allowing the AI to learn from user interactions. This opt-in capability replaces the previous 'Chronicle' function.
details: OpenAI has introduced a new 'Computer History' feature for its ChatGPT and Codex applications on Mac. This opt-in functionality allows the AI to learn from and remember how users interact with their macOS devices, aiming to provide more personalized and contextually aware responses.

The new 'Computer History' directly replaces the previously available 'Chronicle' feature. By analyzing user activity, the AI can better understand workflows and preferences, leading to more efficient and tailored assistance across various tasks.

Users maintain full control over this data, as the feature is strictly opt-in. This ensures that privacy remains a priority, allowing individuals to decide whether to share their computer usage data to enhance their AI experience.
